Geopolitics and the geometry of global trade: 2026 update

Global trade is being reshaped by geopolitical distance, changing industrial policies, and companies' search for resilience. The resulting geometry is more complex than a simple retreat from globalization, because economies continue to depend on one another across critical value chains.

Trade relationships are being rewired

Business leaders can map exposure at the level of products and suppliers, test multiple scenarios, and distinguish structural shifts from temporary disruption. This creates a fact base for sourcing, investment, and market decisions without assuming that every flow will move in the same direction.
